title: Customer activation roadmap — 90-day template
content:
Purpose:
This is a reusable, lightweight 90-day activation plan intended for mid-market and enterprise customers adopting Redwood Inference hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. The doc is a working-playbook: combine with account-specific details in the account tracker (JIRA/Sheets).

High-level outcomes (what success looks like at 90 days):
- Productive integration: key app flows making 10k+ inference calls/day or equivalent (or agreed SLAs).
- Performance baseline established: 95th pct latency meets SLA or documented tradeoffs in runbook.
- Cost profile understood: expected $/1k tokens and optimization opportunities identified.
- Adoption: 3 internal champions (eng/ML/product), recurring usage reports in place, first renewal conversation scheduled.

Primary success metrics (examples to pick/align with customer):
- Weekly active API callers (or team owners)
- Latency P95 (ms) for production workload
- Cost per 1,000 tokens or per-embedding unit
- Feature adoption: streaming, caching, or dedicated pools enabled
- Number of prompts in evals showing no regression

Stakeholders (typical):
- Customer: Eng Lead, ML Engineer, Platform/Infra, Security contact
- Redwood: CSM (owner), Solutions Eng (pre-commit), Performance Engineer, Support SLA Owner

Pre-kickoff checklist (CSM):
- Confirm kickoff date, invite stakeholders, share agenda + workspace
- Provision API keys, access to Redwood Console + telemetry (temp creds)
- Create account folder in Drive (link in account sheet) and seed with templates
- Map success metrics & renewal horizon in account tracker (JIRA: CS-4567)

Kickoff agenda (45–60m):
- Introductions + roles (5m)
- Success metrics & timeline alignment (10m)
content_continued:
- Architecture review: model, endpoint, security (15m)
- Quick live demo: create request, check latency/cost (10m)
- Next steps and owners (5m)

30-day focus: discovery & fast wins
Goals:
- Validate integration pattern (API or SDK) and confirm golden paths
- Identify immediate performance/cost hotspots and mitigation options
- Deliver a minimal observable production pipeline (telemetry + alerts)

Week 1:
- Day 0–3: Kickoff + access validation. CSM to run a guided smoke test with customer (sample prompts).
- Day 4–7: Confirm auth, network whitelisting, and KMS/HSM requirements for Private deployments.
- Deliverable: access validated checklist + first smoke-test report.

Week 2:
- Integrations: instrument Redwood SDK or REST calls into a staging app. Capture baseline latency per model and token usage breakdown.
- Start a short eval set (10–20 prompts) to measure quality.
- Deliverable: baseline dashboard links + short findings doc.

Week 3–4:
- Apply quick optimizations: enable prefix caching, adjust batching, test smaller context lengths.
- If Dedicated/Private: validate resource quotas and autoscale policies with infra contact.
- Deliverable: optimization log + preliminary cost estimate and recommended next steps.

60-day focus: stabilization & adoption
Goals:
- Stabilize latency and error rates under expected traffic profile
- Move key teams from experimentation to production patterns
- Identify feature enablements (streaming, function-calls) that unlock product value

Weeks 5–8:
- Implement model pinning and rollout policy for safe deploys (canary/A-B).
- Create alerting thresholds for SLO breaches and set escalation paths.
- Run a small internal adoption campaign: office hours, how-to docs, and sample app code.
- Conduct a QA/regression run tied to prompt set; document any quality regressions.
- Deliverable: rollout plan + SLO dashboard + adoption playbook for teams.

90-day focus: scale & renewal preparation
Goals:
- Ensure production SLAs are met and cost-savings opportunities are documented
- Create a renewal/expansion plan with next-quarter objectives
- Prepare QBR materials and handoff notes for renewal owners

Weeks 9–12:
- Run performance tuning by workload: quantization recommendation, batching profiles. Document expected delta to $/1k tokens.
- Finalize runbook for failover (model variants, region fallback).
- Collect usage stories and outcomes for the QBR (metrics + qualitative quotes).
- Deliverable: 90-day summary slide draft, renewal brief, suggested pricing/commit options.

Engagement playbook snippets (tactics to drive activation):
- Quick wins email template: short checklist + 1-click test script (attached)
- Office hours: host 2 sessions in weeks 4 and 8 tailored to integration owners
- Proactive alerts: when P95 spikes > 2x baseline, CSM triggers triage with Performance Eng
- Nudge sequences: adoption emails with prioritized suggestions (cache, streaming, smaller model selection)

Risk signals (early warning indicators):
- Low API calls after 30 days (compare to agreed adoption cadence)
- Rising error rates & unacknowledged console alerts
- Security blockers unresolved (network/KMS) beyond week 2
- Key contacts change or lose interest; escalate internally for outreach

Renewal prep checklist (start at day 60):
- Populate renewal brief with: current usage, trends, cost per unit, suggested commitment tiers
- Quantify savings from optimizations done during first 90 days
- Book a renewal planning call 4–6 weeks before term ends
- Include optional expansion opportunities (Dedicated pool sizing, extended observability)

QBR one-pager template (to adapt per account):
- Title: Customer — 90d Activation Review
- Summary: 3 bullets (what went well, areas of friction, next steps)
- Key metrics: WAU, P95 latency, errors/day, token spend, projected $/1k tokens
- Stories: 1 short customer quote + 1 engineering outcome
- Asks: renewal recommendation, exec sponsor ask, product feedback items

Templates (copy/paste starters):
- Kickoff invite subject: "Redwood onboarding kickoff — [Customer] — week of [date]"
- Quick-wins email (to eng lead): "Subject: 5-minute smoke test to validate Redwood integration"
  Body: short bullets: run attached curl snippet; confirm you see tokens in Console > telemetry; flag any 500s.

Open items / TODOs:
- Add step-by-step Private deployment runbook for air-gapped installs (SE to draft) — ASSIGN: Marcus
- Create a small script to auto-populate the QBR one-pager from console metrics — ASSIGN: Engineering intern
- Build a lightweight account-level tracker in Sheets that maps tasks to owners and dates (reference JIRA: CS-4567)

Notes on reuse and customization:
- This template should be trimmed for SMB customers (reduce to 30 days, focused on self-serve).
- For Dedicated customers emphasize capacity planning, autoscale policies, and committed billing early (week 1–2).
- For Private deployments add security checklist before any demo traffic (KMS, IP ranges, audit logs).

Appendix: quick checklist (single line items for CSM)
- Kickoff scheduled & invites sent
- Console access confirmed
- Baseline telemetry dashboard created
- Eval prompts collected
- First optimizations applied
- Rollout/canary plan drafted
- Renewal brief started (by day 60)
